note: Hand-curated, not scraped. `version`, `doc` and `what` are facts taken from Anthropic's docs; `use_when` and `costs` are judgement about when a capability is the right answer for an observed procedure — which the docs do not state and an extractor could not infer. Re-verify by diffing the dated version strings on the tool reference page; a changed suffix means re-read that one page.
planner_guidance: Claude reaches a procedure through one of three doors, and a plan that does not say which one is not yet a plan: the Claude apps (connectors and Skills, enabled by the person, no code), Claude Code (a terminal on their own machine, with hooks and scheduled runs), or the API (something someone builds and hosts). Pick the door that matches who maintains this afterwards. A person who has never opened a terminal should not be handed an API plan.

capabilities.name: Computer use
capabilities.what: Claude controls a desktop by taking screenshots and issuing mouse and keyboard actions. Your application executes every call.
capabilities.use_when: The app has no API and no scriptable interface, and the procedure is visual. This is the last resort that makes an otherwise unautomatable app reachable.
capabilities.costs: Slow, expensive per step, and brittle against UI changes. Needs a machine or VM left running. Treat as supervised, not unattended.

capabilities.name: Browser use
capabilities.what: A browser-scoped toolset — navigation, clicking, typing, screenshots — that your application executes.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure lives entirely in a web app with no usable API. Narrower and more reliable than full computer use when the work is in a browser.
capabilities.costs: Breaks when the site's markup changes. Sites' terms often prohibit automated access — check before recommending it.

capabilities.name: Code execution
capabilities.what: Runs Python and Bash in an Anthropic-hosted sandbox, with file operations. Later versions allow calling your own tools from inside the sandbox.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure involves transforming data — reshaping a spreadsheet, computing statistics, converting formats — rather than clicking a UI.
capabilities.costs: Sandboxed: no access to the user's local files or network services unless you pass data in. Per-cell time limit.

capabilities.name: Web search
capabilities.what: Server-side search run on Anthropic's infrastructure. No server to host.
capabilities.use_when: A step in the procedure is 'look something up'. Replaces a manual search-and-skim.
capabilities.costs: Non-deterministic — results differ between runs, which breaks reproducibility if the output feeds a fixture or a test.

capabilities.name: Web fetch
capabilities.what: Server-side retrieval of a known URL, with a cache-bypass option in later versions.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure repeatedly opens the same page to read a value. Cheaper and more predictable than search when the URL is known.
capabilities.costs: Fails on pages behind auth or rendered entirely client-side.

capabilities.name: Memory tool
capabilities.what: Client-executed tool for persisting notes across sessions.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure's cost is re-establishing context each time — re-explaining a project, re-pasting the same background.
capabilities.costs: You own the storage and its privacy. Stale memories mislead as confidently as fresh ones.

capabilities.name: Bash tool
capabilities.what: Anthropic-defined schema for shell command execution; your application runs the commands.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure is already something a shell could do — file moves, conversions, git operations.
capabilities.costs: Runs with the caller's privileges. Needs a real sandbox or an allowlist before it is safe to run unattended.

capabilities.name: Text editor tool
capabilities.what: Structured view/create/replace operations over files, executed by your application.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure edits files in place and you want targeted changes rather than whole-file rewrites.
capabilities.costs: Only as safe as the paths you allow it to touch.

capabilities.name: MCP connector
capabilities.what: Connect MCP servers directly from the Messages API, server-side. Versioned by beta header rather than a dated type.
capabilities.use_when: An MCP server already exists for the app in the procedure. Cheaper than writing an integration.
capabilities.costs: Community servers vary in quality and are a supply-chain dependency. Auth and scopes are yours to manage.

capabilities.name: Tool search
capabilities.what: Discovers deferred tools on demand so they stay out of the initial prompt. Regex and BM25 variants.
capabilities.use_when: A design needs many tools. Deferred definitions do not invalidate the prompt cache.
capabilities.costs: Adds a discovery round-trip. Irrelevant for small tool sets.

capabilities.name: Advisor tool
capabilities.what: UNVERIFIED — listed in the tool reference as a server tool behind the `advisor-tool-2026-03-01` beta header. Its purpose has not been read.
capabilities.use_when: Do not recommend until someone has read the doc. Listed here so the gap is visible rather than silently missing.
capabilities.costs: Unknown.

capabilities.name: Structured outputs
capabilities.what: Constrains a response to a JSON schema.
capabilities.use_when: The automation's output feeds another system rather than a person. Turns 'parse the prose' into a typed value.
capabilities.costs: A schema that mirrors its own field names invites the model to copy them into the data — validate what comes back.

capabilities.name: Prompt caching
capabilities.what: Caches a stable prompt prefix across calls.
capabilities.use_when: A recurring automation sends the same large context every run — a catalog, a rulebook, a long system prompt.
capabilities.costs: Only helps if the prefix is genuinely stable; a changing preamble invalidates it every call.

capabilities.name: Batch processing
capabilities.what: Submit many requests asynchronously at reduced cost.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure processes a queue and nobody is waiting — overnight triage, bulk labelling.
capabilities.costs: Not interactive. Wrong choice if the person is waiting for the answer.

capabilities.name: Files API
capabilities.what: Upload files once and reference them across requests.
capabilities.use_when: The same document is re-attached on every run of a procedure.
capabilities.costs: Another store of the user's data to manage and expire.

capabilities.name: Citations
capabilities.what: Responses carry references back to source passages.
capabilities.use_when: The automation's output must be checkable — a summary someone will act on, or anything client-facing.
capabilities.costs: Only as good as the sources supplied.

capabilities.name: Agent Skills
capabilities.what: Packaged instructions and assets Claude loads when a task matches.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure is knowledge-shaped rather than mechanical — a house style, a checklist, a way of doing something. Often the right answer when a person insists their process is 'just how I do it'.
capabilities.costs: Does not execute anything by itself. Solves 'how', not 'when'.

capabilities.name: Managed Agents
capabilities.what: Anthropic-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, scheduling, file handling and webhooks.
capabilities.use_when: The procedure should run without the user present — on a schedule or a trigger — and you do not want to operate infrastructure.
capabilities.costs: Runs in Anthropic's cloud, so anything touching local files or a private network needs a different shape.

capabilities.name: Remote MCP servers
capabilities.what: Hosted MCP servers Claude can reach without local setup.
capabilities.use_when: A remote server already covers the app in the procedure.
capabilities.costs: A third party sits between Claude and the data. Check what it can see.

capabilities.name: CLI scripting and automation
capabilities.what: Driving Claude from the shell, scriptable and pipeable.
capabilities.use_when: The user already lives in a terminal and the procedure is developer-shaped. Often the lowest-friction option for someone comfortable there.
capabilities.costs: Local only. Nothing runs when the machine is asleep.

capabilities.name: Claude connectors
capabilities.what: Prebuilt MCP integrations enabled from Claude's settings. The live list is cached separately in connectors-claude.json and refreshed weekly.
capabilities.use_when: The app already has a connector — check the cached catalog rather than guessing.
capabilities.costs: Existing is not the same as enabled. The user must turn it on and grant scopes.

capabilities.name: Leave it alone
capabilities.what: Not every repeated procedure should be automated.
capabilities.use_when: The work is mostly judgement — choosing wording, deciding what matters, reading a room. Or it runs rarely enough that the build cost exceeds the saving. A template, a snippet, or a keyboard shortcut is often the honest recommendation.
capabilities.costs: None. This is the answer that gets under-recommended because it is the one nobody is selling.
